analysis:
The only change in docs/developer/test.md is documentation. Head lines 2115-2131 add instructions for running offline unit tests for the Model Requant Upload workflow (`python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/models -p 'test_*.py'`). The patch shows no executable code, workflow, permission or configuration change. The supplied units are unchanged base text (lines 928-1806) from other sections of the same file, so they add no changed behavior.

The added text describes test coverage: manifest rules, a secret-free preflight, a job in the `prod` environment, master-only runs, a check of both R2 key sets that prints only pass or fail, and an upload gated on this run's check passing. It also covers tools pinned by hash and a selftest that runs before any secret is used. Described as written, these are security-positive controls.

I found no regression against the threat model: provider keys, attestation, App Attest authorization, the prefix cache (T-041), the add-on hold, and fan-helper boundaries are untouched. Nothing here changes TB-011, TB-012 or TB-013.

Limits: the workflow file (Model Requant Upload), `scripts/models/*` and `requant.py` were not supplied. Whether the described controls are actually implemented, such as secret scoping, hash pinning and the master-only restriction, cannot be verified from this documentation diff. The new text is documentation of those controls and no evidence that they are absent. A reviewer of those files should confirm them. The patch also appends the previous sentence's remainder, 'These checks do not establish native model quality', in a slightly awkward position, which is cosmetic only.
